excerpt: Do not take a janitorial bidder's claim of being 'bonded and background-checked' at face value. Use this 100-point weighted evaluation rubric to score competing contractors on third-party client property limits, conviction-clause waivers, W-2 screening, key control, and pricing realism.
quickAnswer: To objectively audit contractor claims on janitorial surety bond coverage, score every RFP finalist on a 100-point weighted evaluation rubric across five criteria: Third-Party Client Property Coverage & Limit Adequacy of $25k–$100k+ (30 points), Conviction Clause Modification & Low Deductible <=$1,000 (25 points), W-2 Direct Payroll & 7-Year Criminal Background Verification (20 points), Electronic Keyfob & Fleet/Equipment Custody Controls (15 points), and All-Inclusive Pricing Alignment at $0.05–$0.15/sq ft or $35–$65/hr with zero bonding surcharges (10 points). Require a minimum score of 80/100 before handing over after-hours master access credentials.

blocks.text: Why Auditing Surety Bond Claims Requires a Quantitative Rubric

When selecting an after-hours cleaning contractor for an occupied commercial office, facility directors hand over more physical trust to the night janitorial crew than to almost any other third-party vendor. Between 6:00 PM and 11:00 PM, cleaning technicians move unescorted through executive suites, open cubicles, R&D workbenches, and reception desks. Yet in 9 out of 10 janitorial bid evaluations, procurement teams award full compliance credit to any bidder who checks 'Yes' next to 'Are your employees bonded?' on the RFP questionnaire.

A simple yes/no checkbox fails to differentiate between a contractor carrying a $100,000 Third-Party Commercial Crime policy with verified W-2 background checks and a broker carrying a $10,000 first-party dishonesty certificate with a strict criminal conviction clause and unvetted 1099 subcontractors. By applying a 100-point weighted evaluation rubric specifically designed for janitorial surety bond and facility security verification, procurement teams can quantify each bidder's protection before comparing monthly square-foot pricing.

blocks.title: Mandatory Keyed-Access Threshold: 80/100 Score
blocks.text: Never issue master keys, 24/7 proximity badges, or alarm disarm codes to a janitorial contractor scoring below 80 points on the Surety Bond & Security Audit Rubric—or to any vendor scoring 0 points on Criterion 1 (Third-Party Client Property Extension).
The 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Janitorial Surety Bonds

Use the five-dimension scoring matrix below to grade every finalist during your janitorial RFP technical evaluation. Require bidders to submit their actual Business Services Bond certificate or Commercial Crime Policy declarations page alongside their ACORD 25 COI.

blocks.caption: 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric: Janitorial Surety Bond & Crime Coverage
rows: 1. Third-Party Client Property Coverage & Dollar Limit
30 pts
First-party employee dishonesty only (covers vendor's own cash, not client's)
Third-Party Business Services Bond with $10,000–$15,000 limit
Verified Third-Party Client Property Crime/Bond: $25k–$50k (<10k sq ft) or $50k–$100k+ (10k+ sq ft)
2. Conviction Clause Trigger & Per-Claim Deductible
25 pts
Strict criminal court conviction required before payout; deductible >$2,500
Conviction clause present, but vendor signs contractual deductible/gap indemnity
Crime Policy pays on police report + badge/video proof of loss; deductible <=$500–$1,000
3. W-2 Payroll Status & 7-Year Criminal Background Audit
20 pts
Uses 1099 subcontractors (excluded by bond) or no criminal screening
100% W-2 staff with state-only check; lacks multi-state or prior-act attestation
100% W-2 payroll verified via Workers' Comp audit + 7-year multi-state background check SOP
4. Key Custody, Badge Logs & Low-Decibel Equipment Fleet
15 pts
Shared anonymous master keycards; noisy uncertified equipment (>72 dBA)
Sign-in paper log for master keys; standard commercial vacuums (67 dBA)
Individual named keyfobs + GPS/timeclock check-in + 62–66 dBA ergonomic HEPA backpack fleet
5. All-Inclusive Pricing Realism & Zero Bonding Surcharges
10 pts
Adds $40–$95/mo 'Bonding Fee' or quotes unsustainable <$28/hr labor
No extra fee, but visit math uses 4.0 weeks/mo instead of 4.33 weeks/mo
All-inclusive pricing aligned to $0.05–$0.15/sq ft ($35–$65/hr) at 4.33 weeks/mo

blocks.text: Auditing Criterion 1 & 2: Third-Party Coverage and Claim Triggers (55 Points)

Together, Criterion 1 (30 points) and Criterion 2 (25 points) account for 55% of the rubric because they determine whether a policy will actually write a check if office equipment vanishes. When auditing Criterion 1, inspect the exact insuring agreement language on the bond certificate or Commercial Crime declarations page. A policy that merely states 'Employee Theft / Dishonesty' without an attached 'Clients' Property' endorsement (such as ISO Commercial Crime Form CR 04 01 or a dedicated Business Services Bond schedule) insures only the janitorial contractor's own internal assets and scores zero points. To earn all 30 points, the vendor must provide at least $25,000 to $50,000 in third-party client property limits for suites between 2,500 and 9,999 sq ft ($0.09 to $0.15/sq ft benchmark), or $50,000 to $100,000+ for 10,000 to 25,000+ sq ft facilities ($0.05 to $0.12/sq ft benchmark).

When auditing Criterion 2 (25 points), demand to see the bond's settlement trigger and deductible. Standard bargain bonds require a criminal trial conviction before the surety pays a dime—and if the policy carries a $5,000 deductible, theft of two $1,800 laptops nets zero reimbursement. Award full credit only when the contractor either carries a Commercial Crime Third-Party endorsement that settles on a filed police report plus preponderance of evidence (such as badge swipe records and hallway video) with a deductible of $1,000 or less, or signs a direct contractual indemnity clause obligating the janitorial company to reimburse substantiated theft losses inside the deductible or pending trial within 30 days.
Auditing Criterion 3 & 4: W-2 Workforce Screening and On-Site Custody Controls (35 Points)

Even a $100,000 Third-Party Crime Policy is worthless if the person vacuuming your office at 9:00 PM is not legally covered by the bond. Under Criterion 3 (20 points), verify two mandatory underwriting conditions: first, every cleaner assigned to your building must be a direct W-2 employee on the vendor's payroll (cross-verified against their Workers' Compensation policy payroll audit). Second, the vendor must document a pre-employment 7-year multi-state and county criminal background check protocol. Why? Because surety bonds include a 'Prior Dishonest Act' exclusion that automatically voids bond coverage for any employee whom the contractor hired despite knowing—or failing to screen for—a prior theft conviction.

Criterion 4 (15 points) evaluates on-site physical security, key control, and operational awareness during evening shifts. High-scoring contractors prohibit shared master keycards, require geofenced mobile timeclock check-ins, and equip their evening crews with quiet, ergonomic HEPA backpack vacuums so technicians maintain auditory awareness of doors, alarms, and late-working tenants without propping security doors open for extension cords. Look for fleets standardized on equipment like the Powr-Flite BP6S Comfort Pro Backpack Vacuum (6-quart capacity, 5-stage HEPA filtration, 11 lb weight with cooling mesh harness operating at a whisper-quiet 62 dBA), the Hoover Commercial C2401 Shoulder Vac Pro Backpack Vacuum (6.4-quart capacity, HEPA media, lightweight 9.2 lb chassis at 66 dBA), or the Atrix VACBP1 Ergo HEPA Commercial Backpack Vacuum (8-quart capacity, 99.97% HEPA filtration, 10.3 lb build at 67 dBA).
Auditing Criterion 5: Pricing Math and Zero Bonding Markups (10 Points)

The final 10 points verify that the contractor's financial model supports legitimate W-2 wages, background screening, and bond maintenance without slipping predatory surcharges onto your invoice. Because a $50,000 Business Services Bond costs a contractor roughly $250 to $450 per year across their entire company, any bidder who adds a separate $50/month 'Bonding Fee' automatically scores zero points in Criterion 5.

Likewise, audit the bidder's labor hours and monthly frequency math using the industry standard 4.33 weeks per month (1x/week = 4.33 visits/mo at 1.08x multiplier; 2x/week = 8.66 visits/mo at 1.0x; 3x/week = 13.0 visits/mo at 0.95x; 5x/week = 21.65 visits/mo at 0.90x). Divide total monthly revenue by total monthly labor hours (benchmarking against the ISSA production rate of 3,500 sq ft per hour plus restroom sanitation at $15 to $30 per visit and breakroom sanitation at $12 to $25 per visit) to confirm the vendor is billing inside the verified $35 to $65 per hour commercial band.

faqs.q: What is the minimum passing score a janitorial bidder should achieve on this surety bond rubric?
faqs.a: Require a minimum score of 80 out of 100 points, with a mandatory non-zero score in Criterion 1 (Third-Party Client Property Coverage) and Criterion 3 (100% W-2 Direct Payroll & Background Screening). A contractor who scores well on price but carries only a first-party dishonesty policy or uses 1099 subcontractors leaves your facility completely uninsured against evening theft.

faqs.q: Why does equipment noise level (such as a 62 dBA to 67 dBA backpack vacuum) matter in a security and bonding audit?
faqs.a: During after-hours cleaning in keyed offices, security breaches frequently occur when technicians working with loud, outdated 78+ dBA upright vacuums cannot hear Perimeter door alarms, intrusion alerts, or unauthorized tailgaters entering behind them, or when they prop secure stairwell doors open to run long cords. Specifying quiet 62 to 67 dBA ergonomic HEPA backpack units like the Powr-Flite BP6S Comfort Pro (62 dBA), Hoover C2401 (66 dBA), or Atrix VACBP1 (67 dBA) improves crew situational awareness and cord discipline.

faqs.q: How do we verify that a contractor's surety bond hasn't lapsed mid-contract?
faqs.a: Unlike standard general liability certificates where additional insureds are routinely tracked, Business Services Bonds often renew annually without automatic third-party notices. Record the bond's expiration date in your vendor compliance calendar and require the contractor's insurance producer to deliver a renewal confirmation certificate 15 days before expiration each year.

faqs.q: Can we require the janitorial company to cover the $500 or $1,000 Crime Policy deductible in our contract?
faqs.a: Yes, and doing so earns full credit in Criterion 2 of our rubric. Include a clause in the Master Services Agreement stating that for any substantiated employee theft loss supported by a police report and electronic access logs or video evidence, the Contractor shall directly reimburse the Client for any loss amount falling below the Crime Policy deductible within 30 calendar days.

faqs.q: How does flooring mix affect the labor hours we audit in Criterion 5?
faqs.a: When auditing whether a bidder's quote supports compliant W-2 wages ($35 to $65/hr) and full bonding compliance, adjust the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr baseline using our flooring multipliers: 1.0x for commercial carpet, 1.04x for VCT/LVT vinyl, 1.05x for mixed carpet and hard floors, 1.08x for engineered hardwood, 1.12x for ceramic tile & grout, and 0.95x for polished concrete.
